claim: Microsoft publishes .NET packages at packages.microsoft.com only for Azure Linux, Debian, openSUSE Leap and SLES; Alpine, CentOS Stream, Fedora, RHEL and Ubuntu publish their own.
quote: Packages are published in the Microsoft package repository at https://packages.microsoft.com/ and are available for the following Linux distributions: Azure Linux, Debian, openSUSE Leap, SUSE Enterprise Linux ... The following Linux distributions publish their own .NET packages: Alpine, CentOS Stream, Fedora, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), Ubuntu

claim: Canonical now owns .NET on Ubuntu; Ubuntu 26.04 has .NET 10 in the built-in feed and 9.0/8.0 only via the dotnet/backports PPA, and Canonical SDKs are always in the .1xx feature band.
quote: Canonical has taken over publishing .NET on Ubuntu. Starting with Ubuntu 22.04, Microsoft no longer distributes .NET for Ubuntu to the Microsoft package repository. ... SDK versions offered by Canonical are always in the .1xx feature band.

claim: Fedora 43 and 44 support .NET 10, 9 and 8 via dnf, but Microsoft warns packages can lag the .NET release.
quote: .NET 10 was released on November 11, 2025. It may take time for the packages to appear in the package manager feeds or for your specific Linux distribution to include it.

claim: Debian 12 and 13 get .NET 10/9/8 by registering packages.microsoft.com via the packages-microsoft-prod.deb.
quote: wget https://packages.microsoft.com/config/debian/13/packages-microsoft-prod.deb -O packages-microsoft-prod.deb ... sudo apt-get install -y dotnet-sdk-10.0

claim: Only openSUSE Leap 16 is a supported .NET target, installed from the Microsoft zypper repo, and its packages depend on OpenSSL 3.x.
quote: openSUSE Leap | .NET --- 16 | 10, 9, 8 ... .NET packages for openSUSE depend on OpenSSL 3.x (libopenssl3).

claim: Mixing distro and Microsoft .NET feeds produces libhostfxr.so / FrameworkList.xml failures; the distros that ship their own packages include Arch, and the fix is apt/dnf pinning.
quote: These errors usually occur when two Linux package repositories provide .NET packages. ... These distributions include: Alpine Linux, Arch, CentOS Stream, Fedora, RHEL, Ubuntu 22.04+. If you mix .NET packages from two different sources, you'll likely run into problems.

claim: Fedora 43 and 44 ship dotnet-sdk-10.0 at version 10.0.110, i.e. the .1xx feature band.
Arch's [extra] repo carries dotnet-sdk 10.0.10.sdk110 plus side-by-side dotnet-sdk-8.0/9.0/10.0 packages.
quote: dotnet-sdk 10.0.10.sdk110-1 (Extra) ... dotnet-sdk-9.0 9.0.18.sdk119-1 ... dotnet-runtime-10.0 10.0.10.sdk110-1

claim: Users hit 'No match for argument: dotnet-sdk-10.0' on RPM distros more than a month after the .NET 10 release, with no timeline given.
quote: dnf install dotnet-sdk-10.0 returns "No match for argument: dotnet-sdk-10.0"

claim: dotnet-install.sh and tarball installs are non-admin but leave you to install dependencies, export DOTNET_ROOT/PATH and update manually; they are the only route to preview SDKs.
quote: When .NET is installed in this way, you must install the dependencies required by your Linux distribution. ... Manual installation is commonly used as part of continuous integration testing or on an unsupported Linux distribution. For a developer or user, it's better to use a package manager.

claim: The .NET SDK snap is provided and maintained by Canonical, giving a distro-agnostic install path.
quote: .NET SDK snap packages are provided by and maintained by Canonical.

claim: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (resolute) ships nodejs 22.22.1; 24.04 ships 18.19.1 and 22.04 ships 12.22.9.
Fedora 44 ships nodejs22 at 22.22.2, i.e. one LTS line behind the current Node LTS.
quote: Fedora 44: 22.22.2-3.fc44 (stable)

claim: NodeSource maintains third-party apt and dnf repositories that carry current Node.js majors for Debian/Ubuntu and RPM distros.
quote: Node.js Binary Distributions ... deb and rpm distributions

claim: mise installs via a one-line curl script into ~/.local/bin (also apt, yum, brew, nix, snap) and pulls tools from multiple backends rather than a fixed list.
quote: curl https://mise.run | sh ... Backends are the package ecosystems that mise pulls tools from.

claim: bun installs from its own script/npm/brew on any distro, needs unzip and glibc 2.17+, and the default x64 build requires AVX2.
quote: The `unzip` package is required to install Bun ... Bun's glibc binaries require glibc 2.17 or newer.

claim: pnpm can be installed standalone without Node.js present, or via Corepack/npm/brew when Node v22+ is already installed.
quote: If you don't use the standalone script or `@pnpm/exe` to install pnpm, then you need to have Node.js (at least v22).

claim: Docker Engine has official install procedures only for CentOS, Debian, Fedora, RHEL, Ubuntu and Raspberry Pi OS; derivatives and distro-packaged Docker are untested.
quote: Docker doesn't test or verify installation on distribution derivatives.

claim: Docker Desktop for Linux is officially supported on Ubuntu, Debian, RHEL and Fedora only, with an untested experimental Arch package, and requires KVM plus GNOME/KDE/MATE.
quote: Docker has not tested or verified the installation. ... Docker Desktop runs a VM that requires KVM support.

claim: Arch's [extra] repo tracks Docker closely: docker 29.6.2, docker-compose 5.3.1 and docker-buildx 0.35.0 as of July 2026.
quote: docker 1:29.6.2-1 (Extra) updated 2026-07-16 ; docker-compose 5.3.1-1 updated 2026-07-07 ; docker-buildx 0.35.0-1

claim: On SELinux-enforcing distros bind mounts fail with permission denied unless volumes carry :z/:Z or are relabelled to container_file_t.
quote: the solution is to use the z or Z flag for volume binds, which will change the label of the files in the volume bind to container_file_t

claim: Layering docker-ce on Fedora Silverblue works but needs manual .repo placement, and Fedora community members point to preinstalled Podman instead.
quote: rpm-ostree install docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin

claim: Bluefin's developer image ships docker-ce with the Compose and Buildx plugins plus Podman tooling and VS Code with Dev Containers preconfigured.
quote: docker-ce, docker-compose-plugin, docker-buildx-plugin ... podman-compose, podman-machine, podman-tui

claim: Rider 2026.1 supports Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 LTS, Fedora 43/44, Debian 13 and Amazon Linux 2023 with glibc 2.28+, installs via Toolbox, tar.gz or snap, and JetBrains flags snap performance degradation.
quote: supported distributions include Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 LTS, Fedora 43/44, Debian 13, and Amazon Linux 2023, with glibc 2.28 or later required ... snap installations may encounter issues including performance degradation

claim: JetBrains Toolbox on Linux is a distro-agnostic tarball you unpack yourself.
quote: tar -xvf jetbrains-toolbox-<version>.tar.gz -C <installation-directory>

claim: VS Code ships official deb, rpm (which also covers openSUSE/SLE) and snap packages; Arch AUR and nixpkgs builds are community-maintained, and Flatpak is not an official channel.
quote: Visual Studio Code is available on Linux through official Debian, RPM, and Snap packages.

claim: Developer consensus is that the sandboxed VS Code Flatpak is unfit for real development and should not be the recommended package.
quote: really shouldn't be the version suggested to users as it's very far from the experience an average user would expect

claim: The VS Code Flatpak cannot see host toolchains, has no easy way to install one inside the sandbox, and cannot reach /var/run/docker.sock by default.
quote: The VS Code Flatpak does not provide an easy way to install a toolchain into the container.

claim: Ghostty is first-party packaged for Arch [extra], Alpine, Gentoo, Nix, Solus, Void and snap; Fedora and Ubuntu rely on COPR/community debs and openSUSE dropped it over Zig versioning.
quote: Arch Linux - official [extra] repository ... Fedora - COPR and Terra (third-party) ... openSUSE has dropped Ghostty from official repos due to Zig versioning constraints

claim: kubectl installs from pkgs.k8s.io apt/dnf/zypper repos pinned per minor version, or via curl binary, snap or brew.
quote: When upgrading kubectl to a different minor release, you must update the version in the repository configuration

claim: Terraform installs from HashiCorp's own apt and dnf repositories on Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora/RHEL.
quote: sudo dnf config-manager addrepo --from-repofile=https://rpm.releases.hashicorp.com/fedora/hashicorp.repo

claim: HashiCorp maintains a first-party Linux repository covering Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/RHEL/CentOS and Amazon Linux only.
quote: the HashiCorp Linux repository ... supports Ubuntu, Debian, CentOS, RHEL, Fedora, and Amazon Linux

claim: Coolify's server-side installer supports Debian-based and RHEL-based hosts, so the workstation only needs docker CLI plus SSH.
quote: Coolify supports Debian-based (e.g., Debian, Ubuntu) and Redhat-based distributions (e.g., CentOS, TencentOS, Fedora, Redhat, AlmaLinux, Rocky, Asahi)

claim: A Coolify Terraform provider exists covering applications, databases, servers and env vars, requiring an API token enabled in the Coolify dashboard.
quote: the provider requires a Coolify API token, and the Coolify API is disabled by default

claim: PowerShell 7 on Linux is installed from the Microsoft apt/dnf/zypper repositories, which is the preferred method.
quote: Installing PowerShell from the Microsoft package repository is the preferred method of installation.

claim: Homebrew on Linux needs a working system C compiler and recent glibc/gcc, is single-user, and uses sudo only during install.
quote: Homebrew does not use any libraries provided by your host system, except glibc and gcc if they are new enough. ... Homebrew does not use sudo after installation.

claim: Which Linux distributions get Microsoft .NET packages is governed by a published selection policy in dotnet/core.
quote: Distributions are selected per the policy defined at dotnet/core #9556.

claim: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS 'Resolute Raccoon' released on 23 April 2026.
quote: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS release date is set for April 23, 2026

claim: nixpkgs is the package set behind Nix, usable as an overlay package manager on any distro.
quote: Nix Packages collection & NixOS
